text: DSH Harbor（DSH 插件，Web 面板与 CLI）：为已安装插件提供带源码出处的能力清单。它在 settings 页面和 `harbor` 命令展示声明与检测结果、运行时注册项、插件冲突、版本差异和扫描变化；升级预检可检查指定 DSH 版本下的入口导入、客户端模块及宿主依赖。适合需要盘点插件或评估升级影响的管理员。无需 API Key；上游检查仅在主动触发时联网。

DSH Harbor is a DSH Web panel and CLI that inventories installed plugins, their capabilities, registrations, conflicts, and version changes. Upgrade preflight checks imports and host compatibility against a chosen DSH version. No API key is required.

DSH Harbor 的功能「插件能力盘点」：扫描 DSH profiles 中已安装的插件并整理检测到的能力及来源证据。通过 CLI 执行 `harbor scan`，可输出文本或 JSON 报告。
DSH Harbor 的功能「声明与检测对账」：将 package.json 中声明的 dsh.capabilities 与扫描结果比较，报告未声明、未检出或未知能力。扫描结果同时附上对账状态。
DSH Harbor 的功能「设置面板报告」：在 DSH Web 的设置区域显示扫描报告、运行时 registry 及插件归属，并提供刷新和更新检查入口。
DSH Harbor 的功能「冲突与版本变化追踪」：扫描同 profile 的工具名、路由、provider 等冲突，比较跨 profile 版本，并可记录插件增删、版本及能力变化。
DSH Harbor 的功能「升级预检」：指定目标 DSH 版本后，为已安装插件检查入口导入、客户端注入模块和宿主 peer 兼容情况，并核对内置 preset 设置。
DSH Harbor 的功能「插件清单草稿」：CLI 可扫描指定插件目录并生成 dsh.capabilities 字段草稿，供插件作者审阅后合并。
DSH Harbor 使用前须知：上游版本检查和升级预检涉及 npm registry 网络请求；扫描核心将跨 profile 漂移作为本地比较，显式检查更新才会查询上游。

@zseven-w/dsh-harbor README · Introduction：

DSH Harbor

Evidence-first governance for the DeepSeek Harness plugins already installed on your machine.
Capability Inventory • Declared vs Detected • Runtime Attribution • Conflict Detection • Version Drift • Change Timeline • Upgrade Preflight
@zseven-w/dsh-harbor README · Introduction：

@zseven-w/dsh-harbor README · Introduction：

The Harbor settings page in DSH light mode — live runtime registries, profile-scoped attribution, local version truth, and the change baseline.

@zseven-w/dsh-harbor README · Why DSH Harbor：DSH plugins run in the host's Node realm with the same local permissions as DSH itself. Harbor does not pretend this can be solved with a score or a badge: it keeps a read-only, evidence-backed ledger of what is installed, what each plugin declares, what its code and live host actually expose, where plugins collide, and what changed since the previous scan.

<table>
<tr>
<td width="50%">

@zseven-w/dsh-harbor README · 🤝 Declared vs Detected：Plugins may declare `dsh.capabilities` in `package.json`. Harbor reconciles the declaration against detection, exposes missing and unknown ids, and fails closed on malformed declarations instead of letting one bad package break the whole report.

@zseven-w/dsh-harbor README · ⚠️ Conflict Detection：The ledger finds same-profile tool names, route prefixes, provider ids, client-module ids, and order-sensitive message hooks. A quoted route used by a client does not make that client the route owner.

@zseven-w/dsh-harbor README · 🕰️ Change Timeline：Snapshots track additions, removals, version transitions, profile moves, capability changes, and claim changes. Even two artifacts exchanging profiles are reported as concrete per-profile transitions.

@zseven-w/dsh-harbor README · 🧷 One Settings Check：The only user-settings check with a known upgrade casualty: when a built-in agent preset is renamed (`code` → `ptc` in DSH 0.1.2) the stored `agent-presets.default` is not migrated and every new session fails. Preflight reports the stale value against the target's preset list.

@zseven-w/dsh-harbor README · How it works：```text
~/.dsh/profiles/*
  ├─ installed package + provenance
  │    registry artifact | link: working tree | file: snapshot
  ├─ declared

The CLI and the settings page consume the same scan core. The default path is offline. Only `harbor scan --check-updates`, `harbor preflight`, or the panel's **Check for updates** / **Upgrade preflight** actions contact a registry.

@zseven-w/dsh-harbor README · Upgrade preflight：```sh
harbor preflight --list                 # dist-tags, recent versions, locally cached host trees
harbor preflight --dsh next             # or a concrete version: --dsh 0.1.5-rc.2
harbor preflight --dsh 0.1.5-rc.2 --json
```

What runs, in order:

@zseven-w/dsh-harbor README · Upgrade preflight：1. The target is resolved (a dist-tag needs one registry request) and `@deepseek-ai/dsh@<version>` is installed into `<state dir>/hosts/<version>` with `npm install -g --prefix`. A completed install is reused; the global npm prefix and your profiles are never written.
2. Every installed third-party plugin's server entry is imported in a fresh `node` child. A `module.register` resolve hook rewrites `@deepseek-ai/*` imports to the target tree, so the plugin links against the version under evaluation while its own dependencies keep resolving from its real install. Missing packages and removed exports fail at link time and are reported verbatim — the DSH loader is fail-loud, so one such plugin blocks the whole profile.
3. `dsh.client.inject` / `external` ids are checked against the packages in the target that declare a web client module (DSH ≥ 0.1.5 skips unknown ids silently, so this never errors on its own). Host peer ranges are matched with npm's prerelease rule.
4. `agent-presets.default` from `settings.yaml` is checked against the target's built-in presets.

@zseven-w/dsh-harbor README · Upgrade preflight：Verdicts distinguish an entry import failure (**blocks boot**) from DSH >= 0.2 rejecting host peer ranges (**blocked by host**, the plugin is skipped). The version gate uses the target host semver library with prereleases included; exact-version risk exemptions are not assumed. **Entry imports** does not verify activation, settings, tools, or devices. Unresolvable/unknown results are inconclusive. Exit code 3 means at least one plugin has not passed preflight or a known settings issue remains. Node >= 20.6 is required for the resolve hook.

@zseven-w/dsh-harbor README · Upgrade preflight：Outside a profile — in CI, or for a package you have not installed — name the subjects explicitly:

```sh
harbor preflight --dsh next --plugin .                        # this repository (build it first)
harbor preflight --dsh next --pack @scope/some-plugin@1.2.3   # fetched from the registry, deps installed with scripts disabled
```

@zseven-w/dsh-harbor README · Contract diff between two DSH versions：Installs both versions into the cache and reports what a plugin could have depended on that moved: packages added/removed, web client modules added/removed, built-in presets, and — by importing each official package's entry in a child — every export name added or removed per package. This is the machine-readable changelog the release notes do not carry; the `settingsNamespace` removal that broke plugins on 0.1.5 shows up here as an export removal in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-settings`. Exit code 3 when anything was removed.

@zseven-w/dsh-harbor README · GitHub Action：Plugin authors can run the same preflight on every pull request and every night against the `next` dist-tag:

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
- run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm run build   # the built server entry is what gets probed
- uses: ZSeven-W/dsh-harbor@v0.1.0-rc.3
  with:

@zseven-w/dsh-harbor README · GitHub Action：The job fails with exit code 3 when the plugin would block boot, warns on stale declarations (`fail-on-advisories: true` turns those into failures), writes a job summary, and uploads the JSON report. The target host tree is cached per DSH version.

@zseven-w/dsh-harbor README · Ecosystem board and release watch：This repository also runs two scheduled workflows: an hourly watch on `@deepseek-ai/dsh` dist-tags that commits a `host-diff` for every tag move, and a nightly board that import-probes every npm package declaring `dsh.bundle` or `dsh.client` (about 4,500 at the time of writing) against the current `next`, incrementally — only plugins whose latest version changed are re-probed, and a full run happens when a DSH dist-tag moves. Results are published as a static page and a JSON index under `board/`. Probing executes each package's module top level in a disposable CI runner; that scan never runs on a user's machine, where preflight only touches plugins the user installed.

@zseven-w/dsh-harbor README · Evidence you can inspect：

Expand any capability pill to inspect its tier, detail, and source evidence — here the Web route registration resolves to src/hub/index.mjs:212.

@zseven-w/dsh-harbor README · Evidence you can inspect：| Tier | What Harbor actually knows |
| --- | --- |
| `declared` | A manifest or filesystem fact, such as client injection or an on-disk realm copy. |
| `runtime` | A registry entry observed in the active DSH host. |
| `static` | A source behavior matched with inspectable `file:line` evidence. |
| `heuristic` | A pattern-based inference that deserves human review. |

@zseven-w/dsh-harbor README · Evidence you can inspect：Harbor reports facts, not a risk score. Spawning a subprocess may be the entire purpose of a plugin; the useful question is whether that capability is visible, declared, attributable, and expected.

@zseven-w/dsh-harbor README · Install into DSH：DSH is a separate package. Install the tested host version if you do not already have it:

```sh
npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@latest
```

For local development, install the current checkout into a Web profile and restart DSH once:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add link:/path/to/dsh-harbor
dsh web
```

For a registry install, use the prerelease `next` tag:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @zseven-w/dsh-harbor@next
dsh web
```
@zseven-w/dsh-harbor README · Install into DSH：Open **Settings → DSH Harbor**. The panel mounts only in profiles with a Web server; the CLI remains usable in headless and CI environments.

@zseven-w/dsh-harbor README · Verify the installation：```sh
curl http://127.0.0.1:3080/_dsh/dsh-harbor/ping
pnpm --dir ~/.dsh/profiles/web exec harbor --version
```

A healthy ping reports four mounted Harbor routes. The package executable is profile-scoped: installing into `web` does not place `harbor` on your global shell `PATH`.

@zseven-w/dsh-harbor README · Capability vocabulary：| Surface | Capability ids |
| --- | --- |
| UI and host routes | `client-injection`, `web-routes` |
| Agent and model surface | `tool-registration`, `llm-adapter`, `global-hook`, `mcp-server` |
| Machine and data access | `subprocess`, `network-egress`, `env-read`, `credential-handling`, `foreign-config` |

@zseven-w/dsh-harbor README · Capability vocabulary：The full, stable definitions and declaration rules live in [SPEC.md](./SPEC.md) and [SPEC.zh.md](./SPEC.zh.md). Authors can draft the `capabilities` member to merge into an existing `dsh` object:

```sh
harbor manifest /path/to/my-plugin
```

Always review the draft. Detection is deliberately conservative and pattern based; dynamic calls can be missed, and examples or dead code can look live.

@zseven-w/dsh-harbor README · Trust model and limits：- Harbor is a **read-only mirror**, not a sandbox, installer gate, or policy engine.
- The default scan never contacts the network. The upstream check is the sole networked panel action.
- Source, manifest, and freshness reads are bounded, regular-file-only, and no-follow; skipped or over-limit coverage is surfaced.
- Runtime waterfall dispatch modes are not enumerable in the current host API, so Harbor marks that runtime evidence as unavailable instead of guessing.
- Static analysis can produce false positives and false negatives. Evidence is for review, not blind enforcement.

@zseven-w/dsh-harbor README · Develop and verify：```sh
pnpm install
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm test
pnpm run build:client

The test runner is compatible with Node 20 and Windows. CI covers Node 20/24 on Ubuntu and Windows. `smoke:pack` packs the real payload, installs it with plain npm in an empty directory, imports the public entry, runs the installed CLI, and checks required files and modes.
